note: The largest pipeline in the country (roughly 1,000 projects under construction or planned) and Dallas is the second-largest market. Gov. Abbott's Aug 3, 2026 directive paused pending data center interconnections until each project passes a PUCT/ERCOT audit, with a report targeted for Dec 10. That pause runs through ERCOT's process, so it does not reach the El Paso, Panhandle and East Texas areas outside ERCOT, and the December target is an audit milestone, not a date when power becomes available. ERCOT was weighing ~474 GW of large-load requests (about 90% data centers) and halted Batch Zero classifications. On Sept 21 Abbott directed TCEQ to stop issuing all data center permits until ERCOT completes its review, and said he will work with the Legislature to eliminate data center incentives. SB 6 already allows curtailment of 75 MW+ loads. The sales tax exemption survives until at least the 2027 session. Water is strained statewide.

rr.n: SB 6 (2025) requires large loads of 75 MW or more to fund interconnection studies and upgrades and allows curtailment during grid stress. The governor's August 3, 2026 letter holds data centers in ERCOT's interconnection process until a PUCT/ERCOT audit, and his September 21 letter directs TCEQ to stop issuing all data center permits until ERCOT completes that review, which is targeted for December 10. The interconnection hold does not reach El Paso, the Panhandle or East Texas, but the permit pause is statewide.

note: Executive Order 2026-03 (May 29) is a review framework rather than a moratorium. It directs executive-branch agencies, excluding higher education, the State Board of Education, the Attorney General, Auditor, Treasurer, Legislature and Judiciary, to apply a higher bar to large data center review, requiring that water consumption not increase and that Great Salt Lake impacts be weighed. It followed the 9 GW Stratos proposal in Box Elder County, whose referendum campaign is now in district court. Dry, cool climate and Salt Lake City connectivity remain positives.

note: Still the world's largest market (Northern Virginia ~13% of global capacity, 0.5% colocation vacancy and a majority of 2026 capacity already committed, per CBRE H2 2025) with substantial power connection constraints: Dominion has quoted 7-year waits for 100 MW since 2024, had ~54 GW under contract by July 2026 and ~70 GW of requests in queue. The 2026 budget left the sales tax exemption in place through 2035 but added a $0.011/kWh electricity consumption tax from July 1, 2026 to July 1, 2028, with revenue above $600M a year refunded. HB 153 requires a site assessment before local rezoning or special-use approval for 100 MW+ projects, and DEQ must define Cooling Water Scarcity Areas by July 2027. The price shown is the unadjusted 2024 EIA average and does not include the new consumption tax.

rr.n: HB 1393 prevents residential cost-shifting for projects of 25 MW or more, HB 496 requires water withdrawal and consumptive use reporting to DEQ, SB 553 makes localities address water supply impacts in rezonings, and HB 153 requires a site assessment before local rezoning or special-use approval for projects of 100 MW or more, with a 500-foot residential setback. The sales tax exemption runs through 2035, but a $0.011/kWh consumption tax applies from July 2026 to July 2028 and DEQ must define Cooling Water Scarcity Areas by July 2027.
